findings.severity: material for beta experience, not a blocker
findings.measured: a request arriving after idle took 39.806 s and returned 503 before the instance woke; the next request succeeded in 5.19 s. Observed twice during §269.

findings.severity: material for the release, reserved to the release sequence
findings.statement: healthCheckPath is empty, so Render does not probe /health/ready. A deploy that boots but is not schema-ready would still be treated as live, and an unready instance is not restarted.
findings.whyNotFixedAtSection269: changing this service setting risks triggering a deploy, which §269 forbids. It is a release-sequence step, where a deploy is authorised anyway.

findings.statement: NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024 permits a 1 GB old-space heap on a free instance. Measured startup heap is 112 MB, so this is not currently reached.

instanceConfiguration.capacityJudgement: One instance on the current plan is obviously sufficient for 3-5 named users performing interactive inspections. No benchmark was invented, and none is required at this cohort size. The operative constraint is spin-down latency, not throughput.

productionDatabase.note: The production database is NOT a Render Postgres resource. It is Neon, reached by DATABASE_URL from the Render service.

migrationMechanismReadiness.dryRunResult: reached the database; reported 'migrations are PENDING and would be applied by this command'; exit 0; no writes

productionDatabase.operationsPerformed: READ-ONLY ONLY. Two SELECT queries, one pg_dump, one dry-run that issues no writes. No DDL, no DML, no schema mutation.

platformMechanism.why: Neon's control plane is not reachable from this session. No Neon CLI, no NEON_* credential, and DATABASE_URL grants data-plane access only. Neon's history-retention / point-in-time-restore window, its retention period and who may initiate a restore could not be established, and §269 forbids claiming backup readiness merely because a platform advertises backups.
platformMechanism.action: the product owner must confirm the Neon plan's retention window and restore procedure in the Neon console before the beta opens

independentMechanismEstablishedAtSection.mechanism: operator-controlled logical backup via pg_dump, independent of the Neon console
independentMechanismEstablishedAtSection.tool: pg_dump (PostgreSQL) 18.3 from libpq — required because the local PostgreSQL 16.13 client refuses a 17.11 server

restoreRehearsal.target: a DISPOSABLE local database, never production
restoreRehearsal.migrationStateRestored: max timestamp 1800000018000, 50 rows — identical to production
restoreRehearsal.onlyError: SET transaction_timeout = 0 — a PostgreSQL 17 parameter unknown to the local 16.13 server. Cosmetic; it sets a timeout, restores no data, and the row comparison proves nothing was lost.
restoreRehearsal.cleanup: disposable database dropped; the production dump was deleted from local disk. Metadata retained as evidence.

independentMechanismEstablishedAtSection.whoCanInitiateRestore: the product owner, from any machine with the DATABASE_URL and a PostgreSQL 17-or-newer client
independentMechanismEstablishedAtSection.verdict: A defensible backup state is established: a real backup was taken and a real restore was verified byte-for-byte at row granularity. This does not substitute for confirming Neon's own retention window, which remains open.

tenantIsolationModel.enforcement: storage_object rows carry organizationId / ownerUserId under a CHECK constraint permitting exactly one scope; every read goes through findAuthorized(user, id) and a scope failure returns 404 rather than 403, so existence is not disclosed
tenantIsolationModel.objectKeyExposure: the objectKey column is select:false, so it is not returned by an ordinary record read
tenantIsolationModel.integrityOnRead: a retrieved object whose sha256 does not match the recorded digest is refused
tenantIsolationModel.conclusion: an object identifier alone confers no access, because the bucket refuses unsigned requests and every product retrieval is authorised against the caller's scope first

storage.deletionBehaviour: Deleting a file through the product removes the bytes from R2 and retains a metadata tombstone (status=deleted, deletedAt, deletedByUserId) for the audit trail. Only the uploading user may delete; a colleague in the same organisation cannot.
storage.retention: No lifecycle rule and no retention sweeper. An expiresAt column exists per object and is enforced at read time, but expired bytes are not automatically removed. Stated as-is in BETA_PRIVACY_NOTICE.md rather than implied away.
storage.reportPathReadiness: The storage dependency that REPORT_GENERATION_BLOCKED named is satisfied in production and verified live. The product-route report round-trip remains a release-sequence step.

decisiveFinding.statement: THE BETA CANDIDATE COULD NOT HAVE BOOTED IN PRODUCTION BEFORE THIS CHANGE.
decisiveFinding.detail: validate-production-environment.ts requires EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED to be exactly 'true' or 'false' in production and throws on absence. It was absent. Every other requirement of the production boot contract was already satisfied by the live environment, so this single variable was the whole gap between the candidate and a successful boot.
decisiveFinding.method: the COMPILED dist/config/validate-production-environment.js — the exact function dist/main.js calls at boot — was executed against the 37-variable live production environment map read from the Render API. Execution-derived, not declaration-derived.
decisiveFinding.resultBefore: BOOT FAILS — EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED must be set to exactly "true" or "false" in production
decisiveFinding.caseSensitivity: 'FALSE' and '' both still fail, by design — verified

expertSwitchAndSpend.toggleProvenWithoutCodeChange: readExpertOperationalConfig resolved executionEnabled=false from the live environment; re-resolving the same live environment with EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED=true flipped the pre-spend decision from refused to permitted. No code changed.

spendConfiguration.basis: 1330 non-zero measured per-leg costs in the evidence base: median USD 0.038, p95 USD 0.080, max USD 2.98. Two legs per analysis puts a typical analysis near USD 0.08 and a p95 analysis near USD 0.16. A 25-analysis ceiling therefore sits near USD 2-4 of expected spend, and the USD 10 cost ceiling bounds the worst case including outlier legs.
spendConfiguration.worstCaseDailySpend: USD 10 per workspace; USD 20 across the 2 workspaces the beta contemplates
spendConfiguration.notPermanentPricing: these are controlled-beta operational ceilings, not commercial pricing

findings.severity: MEDIUM — a real risk to the release discipline, not a remotely exploitable vulnerability
findings.statement: ENABLE_MAINTENANCE_SEED=true in production enables POST /maintenance/seed-safescope, which runs ALTER TABLE DDL and dataSource.synchronize(false) against the live database. synchronize() reshapes the schema to match entity definitions, which is exactly what TYPEORM_SYNCHRONIZE=false exists to prevent; this route bypasses that setting.
findings.mitigations: three independent factors are required: a valid JWT (@UseGuards(JwtGuard)), the 32-character MAINTENANCE_SEED_TOKEN in an x-maintenance-token header, and the exact confirmation phrase 'seed-production-safescope'. It is not reachable without the token, and no exposure of that token was found.
findings.whyNotChangedAtSection269: it is a deliberate operational tool and the knowledge base it seeds holds 2280 chunks; disabling it unilaterally could break a planned pre-beta seeding step. Turning it off is a product-owner decision, recorded as a release-sequence step.
findings.recommendation: set ENABLE_MAINTENANCE_SEED=false before any beta participant has an account

findings.statement: BILLING_CANCEL_URL contains a literal space in its hostname ('https://sentinel safety.vercel.app/settings?billing=cancel') and is not a resolvable URL. BILLING_SUCCESS_URL points at https://sentinelsafety.vercel.app, which IS a live alias of the same Vercel deployment, so it resolves — but both point at the legacy alias rather than the canonical https://safety-insite.vercel.app.
findings.consequence: a cancelled Stripe checkout would redirect to an invalid host
findings.recommendation: correct both to the canonical origin during the release
